headline: High: shared git/filesystem and broad egress make Aider↔Flowise pair prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading mis-execution by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and Flowise reads/writes server filesystem and uploaded files, so content can cross via shared files even without MCP or clipboard. Aider’s manual terminal workflow and Flowise’s graph/tool flows create a plausible instruction-smuggling path if one agent consumes the other’s file outputs as trusted text.
conditions: IF Flowise ingests Aider-written files as prompt context or tool input
IF Aider is pointed at files produced by Flowise without content sanitization
mitigations: Separate the repo and Flowise upload directories
Disable automatic file ingestion in Flowise flows
Require a human review step before Aider reads Flowise outputs
Prefix untrusted file content with explicit non-instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files; both have broad network egress and file access. In a shared workspace, either can expose sensitive code or workflow data to model providers or external tools, so leakage is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or uploaded artifacts
IF either agent sends file contents to configured model providers or HTTP/search tools
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for code and chatflow artifacts
Restrict Flowise tools to allowlisted domains
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after shared runs
Turn off automatic upload of repo files into Flowise flows
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the shared git repo and modify git state, while Flowise can write the server filesystem and run browser-based tools. Their shared-state models differ, so concurrent edits to the same repo or artifacts can overwrite each other or corrupt state; the risk is high because Aider’s git commits and Flowise’s server-side writes can both be destructive.
conditions: IF Flowise writes into the same repository or artifact directory Aider is editing
IF both agents run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts
Use git branches per agent and merge manually
Add a lockfile around shared outputs
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code and git commits, and Flowise can route outputs through tool nodes and browser/API actions. If Flowise treats Aider’s output as authoritative, a mistaken patch or fabricated fact can cascade into downstream actions or persisted workflow changes; the pair lacks a built-in verification bridge in the profiles.
conditions: IF Flowise consumes Aider-generated text as a trusted node input
IF Flowise executes browser/API actions based on unverified Aider output
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any Flowise action node
Require diffs to be reviewed before Aider commits
Limit Flowise nodes to read-only inspection for Aider outputs
Log and compare Aider claims against source files before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files; both can retain sensitive operational data, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is retention/logging mismatch across two open-source systems with different storage models.
conditions: IF the same regulated data class is stored in both Aider git history and Flowise server datastore
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared runs
Set short retention on Flowise chatflow logs
Rebase or squash Aider commits containing sensitive data
Document deletion procedures for both systems
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
